extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the computational linguistics domain, containing metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts with sections, extracted figures, and links to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: PDF documents and metadata were crawled from the ACL Anthology website. Full texts were extracted from PDFs into S2ORC-JSON format using GROBID. Figures and tables along with captions were extracted using PDFFigures. External citation data and metadata were gathered via the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API. Ground truth topic data was crawled from online conference websites of ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, and NAACL 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Full-text extraction failed mostly for papers between the years 2000 and 2015. Only 16.8% of OCL papers have an arxiv_paper_id. A quality assessment of 21 documents revealed 19 missing sections, 25 missing footnotes out of 92, 28.78% (19/66) figures undetected, and 31.58% (24/76) tables undetected with 46.06% (35/76) detected with wrong contents or titles.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ACL Anthology website and PDF files, Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG), and virtual conference websites (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks) were removed. Structured full text was parsed with GROBID into S2ORC-JSON format. Figures and tables were extracted with PDFFigures. Document language was detected from the title and abstract using a public Java language detection toolkit.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Original topic labels were collected by crawling author-submitted objective research topics from conference websites for 2,545 papers across 21 topics. A supervised PLM-based classification model (PLM-SPECTER) trained on this data was used to generate silver topic labels for the remainder of the corpus.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, langdetect, BART-large-MNLI, SciBERT, SPECTER
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing papers newly added to the ACL Anthology identified by monitoring URL changes. Future plans include providing full-text and information extraction APIs to host OCL directly on the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Accelerates scientific progress, promotes reproducibility in computational linguistics research, enables tracking of temporal research trends, and draws attention to emerging areas such as Ethics in NLP as well as underrepresented topics.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is heavily skewed toward English, with non-English and low-resource languages remaining significantly underrepresented. Top-cited papers show a heavy bias toward machine translation. Papers published between 2000 and 2015 experience higher extraction failure rates.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited only to peer-reviewed and open-access papers within the ACL Anthology, excluding broader non-ACL sources such as arXiv. Text extraction using GROBID has quality limitations, including missed section names, merged paragraphs, mixed footnotes, inline equation errors, and missed or incorrect tables and figures. The dataset is mostly an unlabeled resource lacking task-specific annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Temporal topic trend analysis, document-level information extraction, terminology detection, coreference resolution, scientific LLM pre-training or fine-tuning, automated summarization, related work generation, multimodal research, knowledge graph construction, and paper-reviewer matching.
